theory.intro: Recipes, paint and concrete mixes, scale drawings and shared profits all use the same part thinking. Write down the ratio or scale the situation gives, find the value of one part or the multiplier, then answer the question in a sensible unit.
facts: A scale is written **image : original**, so $1:n$ means $1$ unit on the drawing is $n$ units in real life.
Drawing to real life: **multiply** by $n$; real life to drawing: **divide** by $n$.
Do the scaling first and convert the units afterwards, e.g. $6\times50\,000=300\,000$ cm $=3$ km.
To scale a recipe, find the multiplier $\text{new}\div\text{old}$ and apply it to **every** ingredient.
When something is shared in the same ratio as contributions, simplify the contributions to a ratio first.
steps: Write down the ratio or scale the situation gives
Find the value of $1$ part, or the multiplier
Scale up or down to answer the question, using a sensible unit

workedExamples.question_text: A map has a scale of $1:25\,000$. Two villages are $8$ cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life, in kilometres?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Image : original is $1:25\,000$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Actual distance}&=8\times25\,000\text{ cm}\\&=200\,000\text{ cm}\\&=2000\text{ m}\\&=2\text{ km}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A model tower is built to a scale of $1:500$. The real tower is $180$ m tall. How tall is the model, in centimetres?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Image : original is $1:500$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Model height}&=180\div500\text{ m}\\&=0.36\text{ m}\\&=36\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A recipe makes $6$ muffins using $150$ g of flour, $90$ g of sugar and $60$ g of butter. How much of each ingredient is needed for $15$ muffins?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Multiplier}&=15\div6\\&=2.5\end{align*}$
Apply the same multiplier to every ingredient.
$\begin{align*}\text{Flour}&=150\times2.5=375\text{ g}\\\text{Sugar}&=90\times2.5=225\text{ g}\\\text{Butter}&=60\times2.5=150\text{ g}\end{align*}$

(a)
$\begin{align*}\text{Total parts}&=1+2+3=6\\\text{One part}&=42\div6=7\text{ kg}\\\text{Cement}&=1\times7=7\text{ kg}\\\text{Sand}&=2\times7=14\text{ kg}\\\text{Gravel}&=3\times7=21\text{ kg}\end{align*}$
Each box represents $7$ kg.

(b)
Cement represents $1$ part; the whole batch represents $6$ parts.
$\begin{align*}1\text{ part}&=9\text{ kg}\\\text{One part}&=9\div1=9\text{ kg}\\\text{Total concrete}&=6\times9=54\text{ kg}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: Leah, Max and Noor invest $\$2000$, $\$3000$ and $\$5000$ respectively in a business. They share a $\$70\,000$ profit in the same ratio as their investments. How much does each person receive?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Divide each investment by $1000$ to find the sharing ratio.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2000:3000:5000\\&=2:3:5\end{aligned}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Total parts}&=2+3+5=10\\\text{One part}&=\$70\,000\div10=\$7000\\\text{Leah}&=2\times\$7000=\$14\,000\\\text{Max}&=3\times\$7000=\$21\,000\\\text{Noor}&=5\times\$7000=\$35\,000\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: Three friends share $\$360$. Ari receives $\frac{1}{3}$ of the money. The rest is shared between Bea and Chen in the ratio $3:5$. How much does Chen receive?
Ada, Ben and Cara share $\$390$. Ada's share to Ben's share is $5:2$. Cara receives $20\%$ more than Ada. How much does each person receive?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Ada represents $5$ parts and Ben represents $2$ parts. Cara receives $120\%$ of Ada's share.
$\begin{align*}\text{Cara's parts}&=1.2\times5=6\\\text{Ada : Ben : Cara}&=5:2:6\\\text{Total parts}&=5+2+6=13\\\text{One part}&=\$390\div13=\$30\\\text{Ada}&=5\times\$30=\$150\\\text{Ben}&=2\times\$30=\$60\\\text{Cara}&=6\times\$30=\$180\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: An engineer draws a component using a scale of $200:1$. The drawing is $150$ cm long. What is the actual length of the component, in millimetres?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Image : original is $200:1$, so divide the drawing length by $200$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Actual length}&=150\div200\text{ cm}\\&=0.75\text{ cm}\\&=7.5\text{ mm}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A map maker chooses a scale of $1:100$ for an area measuring $6$ km by $6$ km. Explain why this scale is unsuitable for a map intended to be carried.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Map side length}&=6\div100\text{ km}\\&=0.06\text{ km}\\&=60\text{ m}\end{align*}$
The map would measure $60$ m by $60$ m, so it would be too large to carry.

workedExamples.question_text: A $36$ kg concrete mix contains cement, sand and gravel in the ratio $1:2:3$. The whole batch is used, but the required ratio is $1:2:5$. How much extra gravel must be added?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\text{Original total parts}&=1+2+3=6\\\text{One part}&=36\div6=6\text{ kg}\\\text{Original gravel}&=3\times6=18\text{ kg}\end{align*}$
The cement and sand stay unchanged, so one part remains $6$ kg.
$\begin{align*}\text{Required gravel}&=5\times6=30\text{ kg}\\\text{Extra gravel}&=30-18=12\text{ kg}\end{align*}$

foundation.question_text:
A map has a scale of $1:50\,000$.
Two towns are $6$ cm apart on the map.
How far apart are they in real life, in kilometres?
foundation.solution_text:
$6\times50\,000=300\,000\text{ cm}$
$300\,000\div100=3000\text{ m}$
$3000\div1000=3\text{ km}$
The towns are $3$ km apart.

foundation.question_text:
A model city is built to a scale of $1:1000$.
A tower is $240$ m tall in real life.
How tall is the model of the tower, in centimetres?
foundation.solution_text:
$240\div1000=0.24\text{ m}$
$0.24\times100=24\text{ cm}$
The model tower is $24$ cm tall.

foundation.question_text:
A pancake recipe for $4$ people uses $200$ g of flour, $300$ mL of milk and $2$ eggs.
How much of each ingredient is needed for $10$ people?

Ana invests $\$8000$ and Raj invests $\$12\,000$ to start a business.
They agree to share the profit in the same ratio as their investments.
How much of a $\$45\,000$ profit does each of them receive?

Three cousins share $\$360$.
Ola takes $\$90$ and the rest is shared between Kit and Mo in the ratio $2:7$.
How much does Mo receive?

development.question_text:
A bushwalking map has a scale of $1:125\,000$.
On the map, the distance between the ranger station and the bee farm is $45$ mm.
What is the real-life distance between them, in kilometres?

A map has a scale of $1:500\,000$.
Two cities are $75$ km apart in real life.
How far apart are they on the map, in centimetres?
development.solution_text:
$75\text{ km}=75\,000\text{ m}=7\,500\,000\text{ cm}$
$7\,500\,000\div500\,000=15\text{ cm}$
They are $15$ cm apart on the map.

development.question_text:
A muffin recipe makes $8$ muffins from $180$ g of flour, $100$ g of sugar and $80$ g of butter.
How much of each ingredient is needed to make $20$ muffins?
development.solution_text:
$20\div8=2.5$
$180\times2.5=450\text{ g flour}$
$100\times2.5=250\text{ g sugar}$
$80\times2.5=200\text{ g butter}$

development.question_text:
Mortar is made from cement and sand in the ratio $2:7$.
How much mortar, in total, can be made using $7.5$ kg of cement?
development.solution_text:
$2\text{ parts}=7.5\text{ kg}$
$1\text{ part}=3.75\text{ kg}$
$9\text{ parts}=33.75\text{ kg}$
The builder can make $33.75$ kg of mortar.

development.question_text:
Sam, Eddie and Maria invested $\$1500$, $\$5000$ and $\$9500$ respectively when they started a business.
An annual profit of $\$480\,000$ is shared in the same ratio as their investments.
How much does each of them receive?

Adam, Bertie and Cameron share $\$240$.
Cameron receives $20\%$ more money than Adam, and the ratio of Adam's share to Bertie's share is $5:1$.
How much does each of them receive?
development.solution_text:
$A:B=5:1$
$C=1.2\times5=6\text{ parts}$
$A:B:C=5:1:6$
$12\text{ parts}=\$240$
$1\text{ part}=\$20$
$5\text{ parts}=\$100$
$6\text{ parts}=\$120$
Adam receives $\$100$, Bertie $\$20$ and Cameron $\$120$.

mastery.question_text:
An engineer draws a small component using a scale of $150:1$.
The drawing is $120$ cm long.
What is the actual length of the component, in millimetres?
mastery.solution_text:
$120\div150=0.8\text{ cm}$
$0.8\times10=8\text{ mm}$
The component is $8$ mm long.

mastery.question_text:
A map maker wants to draw a map of an area measuring $8$ km by $8$ km, and decides to use a scale of $1:100$.
Explain why this scale is not appropriate.
mastery.solution_text:
$8\text{ km}=800\,000\text{ cm}$
$800\,000\div100=8000\text{ cm}=80\text{ m}$
The map would be $80$ m by $80$ m, which is far too large to print or carry, so the scale is not appropriate.

mastery.question_text:
A $24$ kg bag of dry concrete mix contains cement, sand and gravel in the ratio $1:2:3$.
A builder empties the whole bag into a mixer, but the job needs a mix in the ratio $1:2:4$.
How much extra gravel must he add?
mastery.solution_text:
$6\text{ parts}=24\text{ kg}$
$1\text{ part}=4\text{ kg}$
$1:2:3=4:8:12\text{ kg}$
The cement stays at $4$ kg, so $1\text{ part}=4$ kg in the new mix as well.
$4\times4=16\text{ kg of gravel needed}$
$16-12=4\text{ kg}$
He must add $4$ kg of gravel.
